reason: The code matches technical.md step 4 (internal/amazon/browser.go:352-357 uses any recorded Document response when `errorText` is set). A 2xx main document that Chromium does not render (a download, or a 204/205 with an HTML content type) is not a realistic answer to an Amazon product page. Amazon did answer with 2xx in that case, so counting the check as an answer is a debatable classification, not a proven bug. The comment's claim that the old HTTP collector reported these cases as `request_error` is wrong for the download case: it would have parsed the 200 body. Worth tightening as hardening.
title: Treat a 2xx navigation with errorText as a failed Amazon check
todo:
**Problem:** In `internal/amazon/browser.go:352-357` (`browserTab.load`), when `Page.navigate` returns an `errorText`, any recorded Document response of the navigated frame becomes the loaded page, including a 2xx one. The documented reason for this path (technical.md step 4) is `net::ERR_HTTP_RESPONSE_CODE_FAILURE` for a non-2xx answer with an empty body. A 2xx response with an `errorText` (for example `net::ERR_ABORTED` for a download, or a 204/205) leaves the frame on `about:blank` or an error page, which `parseProductPage` then turns into `price_not_found`. That resets the Amazon failure count.

**Suggested work:** In the `errorText` branch, return the recorded response only when its status is outside 200-299. Otherwise return the failure `Amazon page could not be opened: <errorText>`. Update step 4 of `doc/specifications/amazon-human-checks/technical.md` to match. Add a fixture test: 200 `text/html` with `Content-Disposition: attachment` → `request_error`.

reason: Confirmed: for an empty-body 404/410, `Collect` (internal/amazon/browser.go:100-117) marks the item `unavailable` and then runs `fetchAll` from Chromium's error page. That follows the existing rule: on master the HTTP collector also requested used offers after a 404/410. The proposed fix gives the same `check_error` second-hand status, so the only gain is not sending the two cross-origin requests. Amazon does not normally send empty-body 404/410 pages (its 404 page has a body), so this is hardening for a rare case, not a merge blocker.
title: Skip used-offer requests when the product page is Chromium's error page
todo:
**Problem:** When the product page is an empty-body 404/410 that reaches `load` through the `errorText` branch (`internal/amazon/browser.go:352-357`), the tab shows `chrome-error://chromewebdata/`. `Collect` still calls `tab.fetchAll` (`internal/amazon/browser.go:116`). The two `fetch` calls (`credentials: "include"`, header `X-Requested-With`) then come from an opaque origin. They cannot succeed, may send Amazon a CORS preflight with `Origin: null`, and log a misleading used-offer failure.

**Suggested work:** Add an `errorPage bool` field to `loadedPage`, set it in the `errorText` branch of `load`, and in `Collect` return `SecondHandStatus = "check_error"` without calling `fetchAll` when it is set. Document this in step 8 of `doc/specifications/amazon-human-checks/technical.md`. Add a fixture test: empty-body 404 → `unavailable`, and the fixture server gets no used-offer request (this can share a fixture with the empty-body 404/410/503/429 follow-up).
